subject.title: [Feature]: Cron should distinguish execution success from delivery failure and show warning instead of error

question: Should successful cron execution followed by failed post-run delivery become a first-class `warning` run status, or should execution remain `ok` while delivery failure is shown only through delivery fields and diagnostics?
rationale: Both shapes are implemented by open candidate PRs, and the choice changes public persisted/API/UI behavior for cron status consumers.

options.title: Adopt first-class warning
options.body: Land a resolved version of the broad `warning` status contract after proving storage, Gateway schema, CLI/UI filters, docs, and external-client compatibility.

options.title: Keep ok plus delivery fields
options.body: Use the narrower model where execution remains `ok` and Control UI highlights `deliveryStatus=not-delivered` without adding a new run status.

options.title: Defer the status contract
options.body: Leave this issue open and pause or close implementation PRs until maintainers are ready to commit to the public cron status model.

recommendation.title: Adopt first-class warning
recommendation.body: Land a resolved version of the broad `warning` status contract after proving storage, Gateway schema, CLI/UI filters, docs, and external-client compatibility.

likelyOwner.reason: The current implementation blame and issue timeline point to steipete as the best available owner for the cron status/API product decision.
